SNF Auscultation Rule

Always compare side-to-side and top-to-bottom. A unilateral difference is often more clinically significant than an isolated abnormal finding. Listen at all 6 zones with every respiratory assessment.

Goals of Care
End-of-Life Breathing Patterns
Recognizing active dying in the SNF resident
Why This Section Exists

The SNF nurse is often the first — and sometimes only — clinical presence at the bedside when a resident is actively dying. Recognizing end-of-life breathing patterns allows you to notify families with accuracy, manage comfort appropriately, and document with precision.

These sounds are not emergencies requiring intervention. They are expected physiologic changes. Your role is recognition, communication, and comfort.
